title: "Titanic Disaster - Solutions"
output: html_document

### Introduction:

This exercise is based on the titanic Disaster dataset avaiable at [Kaggle](https://www.kaggle.com/c/titanic).
To know more about the variables check [here](https://www.kaggle.com/c/titanic/data)

### Step 1. Import the necessary libraries

```{r step1, message=FALSE}
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

### Step 2. Import the dataset from this [address](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/guipsamora/pandas_exercises/master/07_Visualization/Titanic_Disaster/train.csv)

### Step 3. Assign it to a variable titanic

```{r}
# the same file is also included in this folder: read_csv("train.csv")
url <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/guipsamora/pandas_exercises/master/07_Visualization/Titanic_Disaster/train.csv"

titanic <- read_csv(url)

head(titanic)
```

### Step 4. Set PassengerId as the index

```{r}
# tibbles have no index; PassengerId is already the first column and identifies each row.
# With a base data.frame you could use row names:
tibble::column_to_rownames(titanic, "PassengerId") |> head()
```

### Step 5. Create a pie chart presenting the male/female proportion

```{r}
# count the instances of males and females
proportions <- titanic |>
  count(Sex) |>
  mutate(percent = n / sum(n))

# a pie chart in ggplot2 is a stacked bar in polar coordinates
ggplot(proportions, aes(x = "", y = n, fill = Sex)) +
  geom_col(width = 1) +
  coord_polar(theta = "y", start = 0) +
  # with the percent listed in each slice
  geom_text(aes(label = scales::percent(percent, accuracy = 0.1)),
            position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5)) +
  # with colors
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(female = "red", male = "blue")) +
  labs(title = "Sex Proportion", x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme_void()
```

### Step 6. Create a scatterplot with the Fare payed and the Age, differ the plot color by gender

```{r}
ggplot(titanic, aes(x = Age, y = Fare, color = Sex)) +
  geom_point(na.rm = TRUE) +
  # set title
  labs(title = "Fare x Age") +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(-5, 85), ylim = c(-5, NA))
```

### Step 7. How many people survived?

```{r}
sum(titanic$Survived)
```

### Step 8. Create a histogram with the Fare payed

```{r}
# create bins of width 10, from 0 to 600
ggplot(titanic, aes(x = Fare)) +
  geom_histogram(breaks = seq(0, 600, 10)) +
  # set the title and labels
  labs(x = "Fare", y = "Frequency", title = "Fare Payed Histogram")
```
